key_facts: The patient is a woman in her 30s
The bruise appeared a few days after a twisting injury to the hand
The bruise and pain have persisted for 2 years
The patient denied any personal or family history of bleeding disorders
Radiography showed soft tissue swelling but was otherwise unremarkable
MRI showed a heterogeneously fluid hyperintense lesion
Pathology showed mixed fibrous and mature adipose tissue with extensive pigment deposition
Lesional cells were spindled, ovoid, and epithelioid with open chromatin and prominent nucleoli
Immunohistochemistry was strongly positive for CD34 and negative for S100, SOX10, HMB45, and Melan-A

raw.rationale: The presence of mixed fibrous and mature adipose tissue with extensive pigment deposition, along with lesional cells that are spindled, ovoid, and epithelioid, and strongly positive for CD34, supports the diagnosis of HFLT. The clinical presentation of a persistent, painful bruise following trauma also aligns with HFLT.

rejected.label: Morel-Lavallee lesion
rejected.why: While Morel-Lavallee lesions can occur after trauma, they typically present as a closed degloving injury with a seroma or hematoma, which does not match the histological findings in this case.

rejected.label: Nora's lesion
rejected.why: Nora's lesion typically presents as a subungual or periungual mass, which does not match the location of the lesion in this case.

rejected.label: Glomus tumor
rejected.why: Glomus tumors are typically small, well-circumscribed lesions that are strongly positive for S100, SOX10, and other markers, which does not match the immunohistochemical profile in this case.
